meta.name: The Bend
meta.vehicle: TBD: LTEC SPV or direct (modeled as a pass-through)
meta.summary: 312-unit 2024-build Class A multifamily, 1909 Greentree Blvd, Clarksville IN (Louisville MSA). $52.0M purchase, $39M fixed-rate IO loan, $16.8M LP raise. Sponsor asks LTEC for >= $1M on a 9% pref / 90-10 side letter.

alternatives.name: Sponsor UW-tab waterfall
alternatives.note: The model's UW Model tab: simple 8% pref from operating cash, operating cash above the pref split 80/20, capital back only from the sale, then 80/20. LP IRR 17.06% (the deck's sensitivity table uses this one).

alternatives.name: No TIF value at sale
alternatives.note: A buyer pays nothing for the rebates left after the sale (every case). The rebates during the hold still arrive.

alternatives.name: TIF rebate cut 50%
alternatives.note: Half of every rebate payment, during the hold and in the value at sale.

alternatives.name: TIF rebate delayed 2 years
alternatives.note: The whole rebate schedule starts two years late (first payment in Year 3).

alternatives.name: No TIF rebate at all
alternatives.note: No rebate during the hold and nothing for it at sale, in every case.

alternatives.name: Through an SPV, fully subscribed
alternatives.note: An SPV invests the check; {manager} commits part of it and manages it, outside members put in the rest at close. Built from {manager}'s SPV template for the current check and partners.

alternatives.name: Through an SPV with warehouse (SV26-style)
alternatives.note: As the fully subscribed SPV, but {levi} warehouses the outside share at close and sells it to new members six months later at par plus 6% carry. Built from {manager}'s template.

diligence.note: Needed for pref accrual (simple vs compounding), order of distributions, AM-fee priority, capital calls, GP removal, and whether a side letter can change the pref/split for one investor. Deck says Reg D 506(c) 'via the PPM'.
Who pays the difference (GP promote only?), MFN, transferability.
Sponsor model has two: Partnership Returns tab (IRR hurdles, compounding: LP IRR 17.086%, deck headline 17.08%) and UW Model tab (simple pref, ops excess split: 17.06%, deck sensitivity table).
Deck Year-1 EGI $5.171M / NOI $3.026M; model $5.178M / $3.033M (loss-to-lease changed). Deck sample distributions ($6,201 Y1) are from the earlier version; model gives $6,240.

Sponsor's rents rest on lease-up: economic vacancy 12.6% (Year 1) -> 8.7% (Year 5), with general vacancy 7% -> 5% and concessions / bad debt 1% -> 0.5% in Year 5, the year the sale is priced on (Year-5 NOI +9.2%). Its Year-1 GPR ($5.02M) sits below Aug-2026 T-12 GPR ($5.16M annualized); a $139/unit 'renovation' premium at $0 cost brings it back. Overall GPR grows ~3.5%/yr from today.

Model adds $3.36M to sale proceeds: NPV at 6% of the 2032-2041 rebates ($475k/yr, $238k in 2041). Needs the TIF agreement: transferable to a buyer? paid as a bond? Without it LP IRR falls (see 'No TIF value at sale').

Model: $650k Y1, $845k Y2 (+3%/yr), TIF rebate $475k below NOI. T-12 taxes $1.33M incl. a $760k Dec-2025 true-up; Jan-Aug 2026 run-rate ~$29-44k/month. Reassessment after a $52M sale? Indiana caps rental property at 2% of gross AV: $1.04M on a $52M assessment (Downside / Stress assume it).
T-12 vacancy loss fell from 16% of GPR (Sep 2025) to 3% (Aug 2026); deck says 95%, email 99%. T-12 NOI $1.79M (distorted by the tax true-up); Jun-Aug 2026 annualized ~$3.17M vs model T-3 $3.12M.
T-12 concessions $210k (model T-3 $228k annualized) vs Year-1 $50k (1% of GPR).
Deck $/unit totals $178,856 vs $176,856; LTC shown ~66.3% but $39M / $55.8M = 69.9%.
Deck: 5-year fixed 5.84%, 60 months IO. Holds past Year 5 need a refinance (refi switch) - the engine otherwise keeps the IO payment.
Deck: funding deadline Oct 5, close Oct 10, 2026; email Oct 14 still >= $1M short. Model assumes close Jan 31, 2027.
LTEC SPV (like SV26) or direct? Modeled as a pass-through until decided.

ui.hold_note: The loan's term ends in Year 5: a longer hold needs a refinance (without one the engine keeps paying interest only).
ui.footnote: Annual-period IRR, as in the sponsor model. At default inputs every line ties to the sponsor model (9-23-26) to the cent: operations, debt, TIF rebate, fees, sale, and the 'Partnership Returns' waterfall (LP IRR 17.09%, 2.06x; deck 17.08%). The 'UW Model' tab's waterfall (17.06%) is the 'Sponsor UW-tab waterfall' variant. No operating agreement received: waterfall terms are as modeled by the sponsor. Not legal, tax or investment advice.

below_noi_income.label: TIF tax rebate
below_noi_income._note: Hold year k = calendar year 2026 + k (as in the model: Year 1 gets 2027's $475k). Years 1-14 = 2027-2040, Year 15 = 2041 ($238k). At a sale after year H the remaining amounts are valued at npv_rate (Excel NPV).

sponsor.label: Sponsor (model)
sponsor.note: The sponsor model's Years 1-8 (rental revenue after vacancy, concessions, bad debt and loss-to-lease; RUBS + other income; operating expenses incl. management fee and taxes before the TIF rebate; lender reserves). Sale at the end of Year 5 on Year-5 NOI at a 5.6% cap.

base.label: Adjusted Base
base.note: Sponsor's rent path (lease-up to 5% vacancy by Year 5) stabilizing 1% lower; concessions $100k / $50k above the sponsor's in Years 1-2; expenses 3% over the sponsor (T-12 runs higher); taxes partly reassessed (+$100k from Year 2); 5.85% exit cap; TIF rebates left at the sale valued at 8%.

downside.label: Downside
downside.note: Lease-up stalls 3% short of the sponsor's; T-12 concessions burn off over 3 years; other income +2%/yr; expenses 5% over the sponsor growing 3.5%; taxes at Indiana's 2% cap on a $52M assessment (+$195k from Year 2); 6.25% exit cap; a buyer pays nothing for the TIF rebates left.

stress.label: Stress
stress.note: No lease-up gains: rents 2% below the sponsor's Year 1, then +1%/yr; T-12 concessions for 2 years; other income 5% lower and flat; expenses 7% over growing 4%; taxes at the 2% cap (+$195k from Year 2); 6.75% exit cap; nothing for the TIF at sale.

custom.label: Custom
custom.note: Starts as the sponsor model. Edit any year, or start from another case.

warehouse._manager_split_note: LTEC's own terms between its partners (issue #9), all off by default. manager_waterfall: all manager cash is pooled; capital holders get capital back plus `pref` first, then each tier gives capital_share to capital holders until they reach to_irr, residual_capital_share above that; the rest goes by fees & promote shares. manager_loans: a partner funds part of another's manager capital; the borrower's manager cash repays it first; recourse = any balance is paid at the end, else forgiven. manager_vesting: fees & promote share vests over `years` from close after `cliff_years`; on `leaves` the unvested part goes to the other partners pro rata.
